deck.caption:
Can an unbroken factory seal lie? Recent reports show counterfeit Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 processors hidden inside factory-sealed boxes using mismatched Intel substrates.

Here is what you need to know to protect your hard-earned money:
• Why factory seals no longer guarantee genuine computer hardware
• How scammers pass basic store packaging checks
• Exact steps to verify your parts upon delivery

Save this post for your next PC upgrade and share it with someone building a system.

Have you ever inspected the serial numbers on your hardware purchases immediately upon delivery?

#HardwareScams #PCBuilding #TechAlert #ConsumerProtection #Ryzen

slides.headline: Factory Seals Are No Longer Safe Proof

comparison_data.left_text: An intact factory seal guarantees a original, working processor straight from the maker.
comparison_data.right_text: Fake Ryzen 9 9950X3D2 chips were found inside sealed boxes holding non-functional Intel parts.

slides.headline: How the Counterfeit Box Loophole Works

steps.text: Scammers obtain cheap or non-working Intel substrate bases
Boxes are repacked and heat-sealed to look original
Sellers pass quick surface checks and ship fake units

slides.headline: Understanding Jargon: What is a Substrate?
slides.card_text: {'title': 'The Base Layer Explained', 'body': 'A substrate is the green base board that holds the processor chip and connects it to your motherboard. Putting an Intel substrate inside an AMD box means the chip is physically incompatible and completely useless.'}

slides.headline: Why Surface Store Inspections Fail

items.text: Outer shrink wrap and security seal intact
Box label matches premium model name
Internal chip substrate matches actual brand specs
